content.text: The campaign is live: it's set to run 21 to 29 November at $55/day, capped at $500 total, with UK and Ireland targeting. I'll check delivery early on, then keep monitoring through the window.
Early numbers: $17.65 spent, 9,918 impressions, 6 link clicks. That's about $2.94 per click, which is expensive. I'll break it down by post to see which ones are pulling their weight.

Two days in: $106.16 spent (about $55 a day), 75,000+ impressions and 39 link clicks, or roughly $2.72 per click. The strongest posts so far by clicks are the "rerun job" post and the "sign up for 60 days" post. The "scores every test" post is the most efficient per click. The "£0 for 60 days" post has only 2 clicks from $6.75 of spend, which is weak but too small a sample to judge. I can't remove individual posts with these tools (only pause the whole line item), so I'll keep the set running and keep watching.

Through 25 November: $213.63 spent, 155,055 impressions, 85 link clicks, about $2.51 per click. Remaining budget is $286.37, and the $55/day pace uses about $275 over the five days left, so the $500 cap should hold. Post-level cost per click is close: $2.36 (sign-up 60-day post), $2.50 (rerun post), $2.55 (£0 post), $2.85 (scores-every-test post). None is clearly losing, so I'll leave the mix as it is.

content.text: The stats API caps each query at seven days, so I'll pull the final day separately and add it to the 21–28 November totals I already have.

Through midday on 29 November the campaign has spent $437.11 of the $500 cap, with 161 link clicks and 293,887 impressions. The campaign ends at 23:59 UTC on 29 November, so I'll wait for it to finish and pull the final totals.

The Black Friday campaign ran from 21 to 29 November and finished at $476.23 of the $500 budget. Link clicks were 179 across 317,668 impressions. X can't see sign-ups, so you'll need to match these clicks against your own sign-up numbers.

**Final totals (21 to 29 Nov, UK and Ireland)**

| Metric | Total |
|---|---|
| Spend | $476.23 |
| Impressions | 317,668 |
| Link clicks | 179 |
| Engagements | 2,228 |
| Cost per link click | $2.66 |

**By post**

| Post | Spend | Impressions | Link clicks | Cost per click |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sign up for 60 days, not 14 (2123748187962542190) | $166.85 | 90,397 | 62 | $2.69 |
| "Rerun job" question (2123566994028154923) | $134.51 | 88,928 | 53 | $2.54 |
| Scores every test, UK & Ireland (2123204606163673400) | $105.69 | 82,600 | 41 | $2.58 |
| £0 for 60 days (2123385800094755076) | $69.18 | 55,743 | 23 | $3.01 |

The "rerun job" and "sign up" posts drew the most clicks. The £0 post was the most expensive per click, but it still performed reasonably, so I didn't cut it. I also made an error in my interim updates: on 25 November I attached the wrong labels to two of the posts' cost-per-click figures. The table above uses the final verified numbers.

**What I set up**
- One campaign, "Nettle CI - Black Friday Week 2026 (UK & IE sign-ups)", billed to the Visa ending 1810.
- One ad group with all four approved posts, objective link clicks, with targeting for the United Kingdom and Ireland only.
- $55/day, $500 total, standard pacing, and the defined audience setting (no optimised targeting).
- Start 21 November 00:00 UTC, end 29 November 23:59 UTC. That's midnight to end of day UK time, since the UK is on GMT in late November.

**Choices you may want to revisit**
- I ran all four posts in one ad group, so I couldn't shift budget between posts. The tools here only pause whole ad groups, not individual posts, so I didn't cut any post.
- I didn't create a separate ad group for each post. That would have allowed a per-post budget split, which might have pushed more clicks for the same spend.
- I optimised for link clicks, not sign-ups, because there's no X pixel. Your sign-up count is the real measure.

**For next time:** install the X pixel before launch. Without it, nothing in this campaign can be optimised toward sign-ups, and we can't report on conversions.
